::: {#exm-double-plus-power-iteration}
#### Unrolling $b_n = 2 b_{n-1} + 2^n$

The recurrence relation and @sol-substitute-once give the first steps of iteration (@def-iteration) for the sequence of @exm-double-plus-power-sequence:

$$
\ba
b_n &= 2 b_{n-1} + 1 \cdot 2^n,
\\ b_n &= 4 b_{n-2} + 2 \cdot 2^n,
\\ b_n &= 8 b_{n-3} + 3 \cdot 2^n.
\ea
$$

After $k$ steps the factor in front of $b_{n-k}$ is $2^k$, and the multiple of $2^n$ is $k$,
so the pattern suggests

$$
b_n = 2^k b_{n-k} + k \cdot 2^n
\quad\text{for } k = 1, 2, \ldots, n.
$$

The initial term is $b_0$, which is $b_{n-k}$ when $k = n$.
With $k = n$ and $b_0 = 0$,

$$
\ba
b_n
&= 2^n b_0 + n \cdot 2^n
\\&= n \cdot 2^n.
\ea
$$

This agrees with @sol-double-plus-power-terms: for example, $5 \cdot 2^5 = 160 = b_5$.

:::
